category_name: Fire detection systems and suppression control
description: All signals converge in the fire alarm control panel, which reliably supplies the responsible offices with all relevant information. Also used to control and monitor other fire protection systems.
Water is the most natural of all extinguishing agents and usually available in sufficient quantities at low cost. Extinguishing effect is based on heat binding capacity.

Sprays extinguishing water very finely through special nozzles at increased operating pressures, increasing surface area for faster heat absorption and evaporation, enabling effective firefighting with reduced water use.

Distribute foam over a large area via foam pipes, monitors, sprinklers or nozzles. Foam covers the combustible material, extinguishes the fire and prevents re-ignition. Suited for flammable liquids or plastics.
Fight fires without side effects or extinguishing agent residue, even where sprinklers cannot reach. Extinguish via oxygen displacement (inert gases) or heat extraction (synthetic gases).
Similar in design to larger extinguishing systems but distinguished by compact design and precise tailoring to specific applications rather than a specific extinguishing agent.

Detect ignition initials in extraction and conveying equipment and generate a water curtain at high speed to extinguish glowing particles. Used where flammable materials are transported pneumatically.
Reduce the oxygen content of the air in the protected area via targeted nitrogen supply, creating a fire-safe atmosphere so a fire cannot start in the first place.
A clear, user-friendly system for visualising and operating fire alarm, extinguishing and hazard detection systems on one interface, ideal for extensive, complex building structures.
